title.analysis: Authentic title "The 3 ETFs That Created More Millionaires Than Any Stock" uses a numbered list ("3 ETFs") with a superlative comparison claim. The script names VOO, IVV and SPY as one S&P 500 exposure, then builds the case through Bessembinder skew, Bogle and SPY history, Buffett's bet and 401(k) data. The "created more millionaires" superlative is not measured anywhere (no count of millionaires by holding). TYPICAL against the cohort. Association only.

script.stored_text_completeness: All 19448 canonical characters read sequentially in full in 2 bounded ranges; auto-generated untimed text; stored ending is complete ("keeps going."); composite characters Bennett and Tessa (ASR also "Benet", "Ben It's", and "Tesla" for Tessa); ASR names "Ted Sieds" (Ted Seides); paid school-community promotion twice; minor duplication ("You You"); audio, timed delivery and editing unverified.
script.opening_words: You have sold something you were right about. Maybe it was a stock, maybe it was a house or a business you almost started or a person. You did the work. You were correct and then you got out at the exact moment that being correct became unbearable and you watched the thing go on without you. Bennett has a whiteboard in his garage for that exact reason. Dry erase mounted between the water heater and a bag of golf
script.ending_words: question was never which fund. Your question is what you would have to build so that being right stops depending on you feeling strong on a bad night. Tell me in the comments, what did you sell that you were right about? I want to know what the room looked like and if you want to keep pulling this thread, in our school community is where that conversation keeps going.
script.analysis: Full 19448 canonical characters read. A narrative essay with composite characters Bennett (stock picker) and Tessa (default index investor): seller's-remorse hook; channel pitch; names VOO/IVV/SPY; Bessembinder skew; index logic; Bogle 1976 and Vanguard structure; SPY creation; drawdowns of big winners; Bennett's 4 a.m. sale; $600/month simulation with an employer match; behaviour gap (Morningstar, Barber-Odean); Buffett's bet; Fidelity/Vanguard mean vs median; target-date defaults; fees and ETF tax efficiency; community plug; counter-arguments (concentration, Big Three ownership, lower forecasts, long droughts, concentration builds fortunes); interrupted compounding; the "four years" payoff; disclaimer; reflective close. Directly verified: Bessembinder 4-of-7 and 4%; Barber-Odean 11.4% vs 17.9%; Buffett bet 125.8%; Fidelity Q1 2026 average $141,000. Inaccurate: funds-of-funds averaged ~3% (2.0-6.5% each), not "roughly 2%"; Netflix's 2011 fall took ~4 months, not 7. The 645,000 millionaires, $32,800 median and several historical details are unverified. Balanced: includes explicit counter-arguments and a mean-vs-median correction. The stored ending is complete.

virality.analysis: Frozen 3672 views / 27.1228 days = 135.38425 views/day. Against 10 peers 0.70659x (TYPICAL); against 5 peers 0.72500x (TYPICAL). Below the cohort median but within the TYPICAL band. The young upload (about 27 days at snapshot) sits among similarly aged peers; one peer ("Are You On Track to Becoming a Multi-Millionaire?") is STRONG. The thumbnail's "BUY THIS ETF NOW!" urgency vs the reflective script is a possible mismatch; no CTR or retention data to test it.
